transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

A fridge that sits around 10°C while the freezer stays cold is almost always an airflow problem in a frost-free model. These appliances have one cooling coil in the freezer; a fan pushes the cold air into the fridge through vents at the back. If those vents are blocked by ice (often caused by a failed defrost system) or if the fan stops, the freezer stays cold but the fridge warms up. Before we go further, please do two quick checks:
1. Check the temperature settings: Ensure neither compartment is set to a 'holiday' or 'eco' mode and that the dials/display are set to standard (fridge around 3–5°C, freezer -18°C).
2. Check for ice blockage: Open the freezer door and look at the back interior wall. Is there a solid layer of frost or ice covering the coils? Also, listen carefully when the door is closed – do you hear a faint hum or whirring (the fan) running? Please let me know what you see regarding the ice and whether you can hear the fan.

Thanks. The dial inside is on 3 of 5, no eco or holiday mode that I can see. There's some frost on the back of the freezer but not loads, and I can hear it running quite a lot. Fridge thermometer says 10C and freezer -16C.

1. Check for water: Look at the bottom of the fridge compartment (behind the vegetable drawer if there is one). Is there any standing water or dampness, or is it completely dry? This helps us decide whether to try clearing a drain hole first or move straight to a full manual defrost.
I'm not sure, I haven't looked at the bottom of the fridge. I'll have a look, but I don't think I've noticed any water. Is that the right thing to check?

Yes, that is exactly the right thing to check. The cold air travels from the freezer into the fridge through vents at the back. During the automatic defrost cycle, any ice on the cooling coils melts and drains away through a small hole at the bottom of the compartment. 1. 2. That standing water can freeze into a block of ice behind the back panel, physically blocking the airflow vents. This stops cold air from reaching the fridge section, causing it to warm up while the freezer stays cold. Please check if there is any water or dampness at the bottom of the fridge compartment.

I haven't had a proper look at the bottom of the fridge yet, so I can't say either way. I can't pull the fridge out of the cabinet, as it's screwed in and it's the landlord's. Is there anything else I can check from the front?

Since you cannot move the appliance or access the internal components due to the installation, checking for water at the bottom is difficult without risking damage or mess. The most effective check you can perform from the front is a full manual defrost. The symptoms (fridge warm, freezer cold, fan running) strongly suggest that ice has built up inside the insulation or behind the panels, blocking the airflow to the fridge section. This is often caused by a defrost system fault (like a heater or thermostat failing), which lets ice accumulate until it chokes the vents. Please switch the appliance off at the wall socket. Remove all food into cool bags with ice packs, place towels inside both compartments to catch melting ice, and leave the doors wide open for 24 hours. After this time, ensure everything is completely dry before switching it back on. This will confirm if the issue is simply a blockage that needs clearing (which may recur) or if there is a deeper fault requiring an engineer.

Ok, I can do a full defrost but I'd have to empty everything out first, so I haven't tried it yet. Is it worth doing that, or should I report it to the letting agent first? Also the model is a Hotpoint HMCB 7030 AA if that helps.

Yes, you should report it to your letting agent. Because this is a rented property and the appliance is integrated (screwed into the kitchen), you are not responsible for dismantling it or replacing internal parts like the heater or thermostat. The symptoms—fridge warm at 10°C while the freezer stays cold, with the fan running—are classic signs of a defrost system fault. The automatic heating cycle that melts frost off the cooling coils has likely failed (usually due to a faulty heater or thermostat). This allows ice to build up inside the unit, blocking the airflow from the freezer into the fridge. 1. 2. 3. This indicates a likely failure of the defrost system components inside the unit. They will need to arrange for an engineer to diagnose and replace the faulty part (likely the heater or thermostat). A manual defrost might temporarily cool the fridge again, but it will warm up once more as soon as the ice rebuilds.
